North Providence weighs $500,000 facade grant for Centerdale, Merrillville businesses
The town's CDBG project manager said the facade program could give qualifying small businesses as much as $50,000 each, pending state funding approval.
The North Providence Planning Board held a public hearing Thursday, Oct. 14, on proposed community development block grant projects, including a facade improvement program for small businesses.
THE PROPOSAL Maria Rosa Zakuma, identified as CDBG project manager for North Providence, told the board the town is competing for a share of more than $1 million available from the state in this grant cycle. She said one proposal would fund facade improvements for low- and moderate-income commercial areas in Centerdale and Merrillville.
Zakuma said the money could cover things like "a better uh publish or add announcements and the entry it will be maybe windows or doors or maybe a sidewalk to get inside the building perhaps and it will be a code violation."
FUNDING AMOUNT Asked what dollar figure the town would seek, Zakuma said "it will be like uh 500,000 that will be fine and we can be able to give them to each one of the businesses maybe perhaps as much as 50,000."
Board member Steve Patassi asked whether the funds would go toward sidewalks or lighting. Zakuma clarified the money is meant for private small businesses in qualifying low- to moderate-income census areas, citing the example of "the little bakery down the street" or "a hair salon."
NO BOARD VOTE Chairman Dave Pari noted the board was not voting on the proposal. "So they're not voting on anything. This is just a public hearing," he said.
Zakuma said the next step is a second public hearing Nov. 3, where a resolution would be considered. No members of the public spoke during the hearing on this item.
